name: Barbell Medicine
who: Jordan Feigenbaum, MD and Austin Baraki, MD host the Barbell Medicine Podcast; the pair's clinic sells 1:1 coaching in fitness, nutrition, and injury/rehab plus group programming.
why: Physician-led team of 15+ named coaches gives a rare combo of medical credibility and a real individualized coaching business behind the show.
takeaway: Pair medical credentials with a named coaching team — credibility plus real capacity to serve clients.

name: Renaissance Periodization (RP Strength)
who: Dr. Mike Israetel fronts RP's YouTube channel and frequent podcast guest appearances; RP sells the RP Hypertrophy App and RP Diet Coach App, self-adjusting coaching apps he co-authored.
why: App-scale coaching business built directly on his own periodization research, with one of the largest audiences in evidence-based lifting media.

name: Legion Athletics / Muscle for Life (Mike Matthews)
who: Mike Matthews hosts the long-running Muscle for Life podcast and runs Legion's 1:1 body-transformation coaching: custom plans, weekly check-in calls, and video form review.
why: Documented scale (Legion claims 5,010+ coaching clients, 91% reporting goal success) backed by weekly-check-in coaching, not just templated plans.
reach: Podcast top health-charts regular · IG ~350K approx (unverified 2026-08)
takeaway: Weekly check-in calls and video form review beat a template — real feedback loops keep clients.

name: Revive Stronger (Steve Hall)
who: Steve Hall hosts the Revive Stronger Podcast; Revive Stronger sells online physique coaching with tailored programs and video check-ins, run by a small coaching team.
why: Coaching is genuinely evidence-based and personally delivered, and Hall backs it with his own WNBF pro card (2024) as a natural bodybuilder.
takeaway: Earn your own pro card while you coach — walking the walk backs the evidence-based claims.

name: Sigma Nutrition (Danny Lennon)
who: Danny Lennon hosts Sigma Nutrition Radio; Sigma Nutrition's coaching team of four works directly with pro MMA fighters, boxers, and powerlifters on nutrition.
why: Niche but credible: real paying coaching page, a genuine coach team, and clients who are verifiable competitive athletes.
takeaway: Go niche and credible — a small team serving verifiable pro athletes beats broad, unproven reach.

name: Danny Matranga (Dynamic Dialogue)
who: Danny Matranga hosts the 400+ episode Dynamic Dialogue podcast; sells app-based training plus 1:1 coaching with Coach Danny and his coaching team.
why: Combines a consistent twice-weekly educational show with a real named coaching team, not just a self-serve app.
takeaway: Show up twice a week, every week — consistency in a long-running show builds the audience that buys.

name: Squat University (Dr. Aaron Horschig)
who: Dr. Aaron Horschig, DPT, hosts the Squat University podcast and runs a namesake coaching program bridging physical therapy and strength coaching.
why: A licensed doctor of physical therapy running an actual clinical/coaching program gives rare credibility on top of a large following.
takeaway: Bridge physical therapy and strength coaching — treating injuries and building strength in one practice.

name: Mind Pump Media
who: Sal Di Stefano, Adam Schafer, and Justin Andrews host the Mind Pump podcast; they sell MAPS training programs and a trainer-facing coaching certification course.
why: One of the biggest fitness podcasts for a decade; the coaching product is real but leans templated (MAPS programs) rather than deeply individualized.
takeaway: Certify trainers in your system — teaching the method scales further than templated programs alone.

name: Barbell Shrugged / Shrugged Collective
who: Anders Varner and Doug Larson host the long-running Barbell Shrugged podcast; Shrugged Collective sells its Program Vault training programs and, per its own site, now partners with RAPID Health Optimization to coach elite athletes and executives.
why: The RAPID Health Optimization partnership adds a genuine high-end coaching arm on top of what would otherwise be templated program sales.
takeaway: Partner with a specialist coaching brand to add a real coaching arm to your templated products.

name: Brains and Gains (Dr. David Maconi)
who: Dr. David Maconi hosts the Brains and Gains podcast; he sells coaching through his own site and coaches through the Boostcamp app.
why: Smallest, most niche pass on this list, but the coaching product is real and named, not just a supplement funnel.

handles.podcast: Brains and Gains with Dr. David Maconi

takeaway: Keep the coaching product real and named, even at small scale — never let it become a supplement funnel.

name: Layne Norton (BioLayne)
who: Dr. Layne Norton produces the BioLayne YouTube/podcast content and co-founded the Carbon diet-coaching app, which delivers algorithm-driven personalized nutrition coaching.
why: PhD in Nutritional Sciences plus an elite competitive record in powerlifting and natural bodybuilding, paired with a coaching app he actually authored.

name: Jordan Syatt (Syatt Fitness)
who: Jordan Syatt is a widely followed fitness content creator (former Tony Robbins strength coach) who sells individualized 1:1 online coaching combining nutrition and strength programming.
why: Practical, no-nonsense coaching brand with a real 'I take care of all the thinking for you' 1:1 service behind a large content following.

name: GDFIT (Greg Doucette)
who: Greg Doucette is one of fitness YouTube's largest personalities; his GDFIT app sells structured, semi-personalized training and nutrition coaching plans.
why: Huge reach and a real coaching app, but the coaching leans templated/algorithmic rather than a human check-in relationship, so it scores at the lower end of the coaching gate.
takeaway: Reach alone isn't coaching — semi-personalized templates still need a real path toward genuine feedback.

name: Nerd Fitness (Steve Kamb)
who: Steve Kamb built Nerd Fitness into a long-running fitness media brand (blog, newsletter, YouTube); Nerd Fitness Coaching pairs clients with real human coaches for multiple weekly check-ins and video form review.
why: One of the oldest continuously-running online coaching operations in the space (since 2009), with a genuinely documented human check-in process, not just an app.
takeaway: Keep a human check-in process running for over a decade — longevity beats novelty in coaching.
